convoLines.text: "Can I tell you something? I stole medicine from the stash once and never confessed."
Evelyn has an edge today — something curdled.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what they confided. You'd know about that."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Don't tell anyone I told you. What's on your mind?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Since Maya died... I keep expecting to see Maya at the fire. Stupid."
"I keep turning over the last thing Maya said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Evelyn grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Evelyn is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Sure. I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"What did you do for fun? Before. The thing you'd do on a perfect Saturday."
"The free things. Turns out they were the expensive ones."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on what you did for fun."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"I've seen worse. I haven't, but saying it helps."
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. Meet me at the creek bend, past the treeline and we'll fill packs before dark."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"We were just talking. Nothing important."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Evelyn nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Maya is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Sleep's gone strange. I tend the fire without being asked at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
You show them Sassafras — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.

"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we got cut off, 4 days back. 'You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.' We still owe what they confided a proper ending, too. …if that makes sense."
"The fire'll settle it. It settles everything, eventually."
"My part? I oil boots on rest days and stay neutral until there's a winner."
"Still on what's been happening. …sorry."

"Alright. Catch you later."

"This was good." They mean it.
"You said fun was just being around your people. Do we count? Are we trying?"
They nod. "Okay."
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.

"Still on that personal stuff."
